title: Leslie Cross: the letters
text: Until 1951, veganism had no clear formal definition. Leslie Cross was the person who set out to define what veganism actually meant, and wrote the letters that gave it one. He and others spent years working on the wording, carefully guarding the principle from drifting into the language of welfare or reducing harm. They knew that once a definition was loose, the meaning would slip with it. In 1951 the Vegan Society's object became to end the exploitation of animals by man, and the word veganism came to mean the doctrine that man should live without exploiting animals. Not so much welfare, Cross wrote, as liberation, because the relationship is in the main one of master and slave, and it has to be abolished before something better and finer can be built.
